data.gender_notes: Sarvagya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has acquired all knowledge. The name Sarvagya carries the meaning “All Knowing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sarvagya usually hope their child will grow to embody all knowing and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sarvagya belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “All Knowing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sarvagya total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sarvagya" carries the profound significance of wisdom and knowledge. In Hindu culture, a person named Sarvagya is often perceived as an enlightened individual who has acquired vast knowledge and understanding of the world and the universe. Such individuals are typically respected and revered within their communities. They may be recognized for their wisdom in various fields such as philosophy, science, mathematics, or spirituality.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Sarvagya" also has deep spiritual significance as it implies a state of realization and enlightenment. According to Hindu philosophy, Sarvagya is a person who has transcended worldly desires and attained a state of pure knowledge, awareness, and self-realization. This intense focus on knowledge and wisdom aligns with the Hindu pursuit of Moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. A Sarvagya person embodies the spirit of constant learning and strives to expand their awareness and understanding of the universe, helping them to lead a meaningful and fulfilling spiritual life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sarvagya: One who possesses omniscience, transcending all limitations of space and time. A seeker of absolute knowledge, enlightened and wise.

vedic_reference.note: Rooted in the Vedic tradition and mythology, Sarvagya refers to one who has attained omniscience or all-knowingness, a common trait among various Hindu deities and revered figures.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sarvagya was a sage mentioned in the Mahabharata The name Sarvagya carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Sarvagya was a sage who possessed the divine gift of omniscience, and was consulted by Bhishma Pitamaha for guidance during the Kurukshetra war.
